about: Every wind constant in plandscape/wind (TECHNIQUES §34): a URL and a verbatim quote, or design=true. Quotes were read from the fetched page or PDF text; [EPMC]/[XREF] mean the abstract came through the Europe PMC or Crossref API.

BEAUFORT.quote: 3 7-10 Gentle Breeze ... Leaves and small twigs constantly moving, light flags extended
BEAUFORT.note: knot bands of forces 0-12 from this table; m/s = band midpoint x 0.5144; force 12 '64+' taken at 66 kn

LAND.quote: 6 22-27 Strong Breeze ... Larger tree branches moving, whistling in wires
LAND.note: every land description is copied from the 'On Land' column

Z0_OPEN.quote: Level country with low vegetation (e.g. grass)

CANOPY_A.quote: 1.0 - 1.1 for larch and small evergreen trees
CANOPY_A.note: M = Mc exp[a(z/hc - 1)], valid for 0.5 hc <= z <= hc; used for broadleaves too (no broadleaf value found)

SIGMA_U.quote: flat and homogeneous terrain σu u∗⁻¹ = 2.4 (e.g. Panofsky and Dutton, 1984)
SIGMA_U.note: and 'roughness sub-layer flows above canopies given by Raupach et al. (1996) (1.7)'

KAIMAL.quote: Kaimal is valid in range from 0.002 Hz to 0.3 Hz
KAIMAL.note: the field extends to 1.2 Hz so limbs and grass see buffeting; the spectral shape above 0.3 Hz is an extrapolation

DAVENPORT_CY.note: lateral coherence decay; the exponential form is Davenport's, C_y = 7 is a design value

CONVECTION.note: gusts advect at the canopy-top mean speed (Taylor's frozen turbulence)

WOOD.note: USDA Wood Handbook (FPL-GTR-113) Table 4-3a, Green rows: specific gravity and modulus of elasticity (MPa). Also: Loblolly Green 0.47 50,000 9,700; Longleaf Green 0.54 59,000 11,000; Sweetgum Green 0.46 49,000 8,300; Yellow-poplar Green 0.40 41,000 8,400; Baldcypress Green 0.42 46,000 8,100; Live Green 0.80 82,000 10,900; Water Green 0.56 61,000 10,700; Southern [magnolia] Green 0.46 47,000 7,700

WOOD_DEFAULT.note: dogwood and redbud are not tabulated: hardwood mean

MC_GREEN.note: green moisture content 80 % of dry mass

LEAF_FRACTION.quote: the mean f0 increased by 19.4% in winter … L = 1.18 ± 0.12
LEAF_FRACTION.note: calibrated: 0.09 gives a mean bare/leafy f0 ratio of 1.20 over the seven deciduous species

ZETA_LEAFY.quote: summer damping ratio to be 8.6 ± 2.2% and the winter damping ratio to be 3.9 ± 1.3%

ZETA_BARE.quote: summer damping ratio to be 8.6 ± 2.2% and the winter damping ratio to be 3.9 ± 1.3%

ZETA_BRANCH.quote: Values of 4.5% (low amplitudes) to 7.5% (high amplitudes) could be generated for Branch 1.

VOGEL_B.quote: F ∝ U∞^(2+V), where F is the drag force… and V the Vogel exponent
VOGEL_B.note: Table 1: Pinus taeda -1.1 (Vogel 1989); tuliptree leaf 'V ∼ −1'; dense poroelastic structures 'approaches V ∼ −1'

CD_20.quote: At 20 m/s they ranged from 0.15 to 0.22
CD_20.note: Vollsinger et al. 2005, crown drag coefficients of hardwoods; midpoint 0.185

U0.note: speed scale of streamlining in F = ½ρ C_d0 A U² (1 + U/U0)^b

FLUTTER_HZ.quote: The leaf mode… has a more localized topos and a higher frequency chronos PSD (about 8 Hz).
FLUTTER_HZ.note: Table 1 gives the leaf torsional frequency 6 ± 1 Hz; 'weak dependence of leaf flutter on wind velocity'

TRUNK_CHECK.quote: The trunk damping, when all branches are attached, was ζ = 10.6% at a natural frequency of 0.34 Hz.
TRUNK_CHECK.note: open-grown silver maple, 19.7 m: plotted against our Rayleigh f0 (gallery wind.jpg)

BRANCH_CHECK.quote: The frequency increased from 0.33 Hz to 1.0 Hz
BRANCH_CHECK.note: an isolated branch sways ~3x the trunk; ours come out 1.4-3x

BRANCH_RATIO.quote: a modal frequency ratio between the trunk mode and the branch mode near 1:2, a branch damping rate larger than 0.2

CANTILEVER.quote: a cantilever beam approximation adequately predicts the fundamental frequency of conifers, but not that of broadleaf trees
CANTILEVER.note: why f0 is a whole-tree Rayleigh quotient here, not a DBH/H² formula

ELASTIC_SIMILARITY.note: d = c L^{3/2} after McMahon & Kronauer (1976), c calibrated per tree on its own trunk; the exponent is from that literature, recalled not fetched

WIND_SEASON.note: default directions: southerly spring/summer, NE fall, NW winter
